Alaska.Ai — The Stack

2026-06-03 · branch claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-03
⚠ No defensible target this cycle — 2026-06-03

The Stack ran its full four-category scan for 2026-06-03. Eight candidate mechanisms were surfaced across facilities, vehicles, capital/sovereignty, and regulatory categories. None cleared all seven gates of the anti-confabulation gate. The 21-day window broadening was applied; no additional candidates survived. No post was written, no image was rendered.

Validation note

14-day window (May 20–June 3) and 21-day broadening window (May 13–June 3) both exhausted. Eight candidates evaluated across all four mechanism categories. No candidate passed all seven gates. Window was broadened to 21 days within the same mapper run; no additional candidates survived. The two most developed candidates (C1 GCI fiber, C8 LNG jurisdiction gap) came closest but failed Gate 3 and Gate 5 respectively. C8 in particular has a structurally sound mechanism but its claimed chokepoint resolves to a multi-member commission (FERC, RCA, or legislature) at every layer. The validator did not lower the bar to force a selection.

Dropped mechanisms (8 candidates)

Mechanism Gate failure reason
GCI AU-Aleutians Subsea Fiber Infrastructure System
facilities · trigger: 2026-05-27		 missing_primary_source_per_layer — FCC cable landing license settlement URL (L2) returned HTTP 503 on two independent fetch attempts; Layer 3 (GCI unilateral repair authority) sourced only to news articles with no contract, org chart, or official document establishing the claimed dispatch authority; Layers 4 and 5 also lack primary sources beyond news articles. Removing L2 breaks the FCC regulatory layer of the chain. Gate 3 fails.
DAF Alaska Enhanced Use Lease Three-Base AI Data Center Program
facilities · trigger: 2026-05-05		 no_news_tie — The ClearanceJobs article (April 14, 2026) and Air and Space Forces Magazine article (April 11, 2026) are both outside the 14-day window. No in-window (May 20–June 3) published news article about the May 29 Alaska-specific EUL proposal deadline or submissions was found on Breaking Defense, Federal News Network, Data Center Dynamics, or ADN. The deadline event is in-window but an event alone without a published news article covering it does not satisfy Gate 1.
Alaska BEAD Subgrantee Grant Execution Stack (GCI-Quintillion Novation Gate)
vehicles · trigger: 2026-04-22		 no_news_tie — ADN April 22, 2026 trigger is 42 days before the run date, outside the 21-day broadening window. The GCI Aleutians fiber break articles are in-window but address cable repair, not BEAD subgrantee novation mechanics.
AIDEA Section 1002 Area Capital Deployment Gate
capital_sovereignty · trigger: 2026-05-15		 no_ak_consequence — The AI connection claimed is that seismic data from Arctic refuge oil exploration will inform future North Slope AI infrastructure siting decisions. This is too attenuated to satisfy Gate 4's requirement for a concrete Alaska AI consequence reducible to sector + decision/risk + named actor + timeframe. The mechanism itself concerns Arctic oil exploration capital deployment. 21-day broadening window applied; still fails Gate 4.
APFC FY27 Investment Policy Statement Adoption Gate
capital_sovereignty · trigger: 2026-05-28		 no_ak_consequence and diffuse_chokepoint — Gate 4 fails: no concrete Alaska AI industry consequence can be named; a 1% reduction in a globally diversified $86B fund's PE allocation does not trace to a specific Alaska AI sector decision or named actor. Gate 5 also fails: the IPS adoption requires a board vote, making it a committee decision not a single-officer binary.
SBA Tribal 8(a) New-Entrant Application Freeze — ONAA Vacancy Gate
capital_sovereignty · trigger: 2026-05-14		 recent_repeat — The May 25 post already anatomized 'ANC 8(a) Sole-Source Federal Contracting Pipeline — SBA Application Gate and Corporate Subsidiary Stack.' The underlying mechanism (SBA 8(a) program, application processing gate, ANC participation) substantially overlaps the prior anatomy's layer chain. Gate 7 fails.
Alaska Railbelt OATT — RCA Docket U-25-028
regulatory · trigger: 2025-09-18		 no_news_tie — The RCA What's New page (fetched June 3, 2026) contains no entries for docket U-25-028 or OATT in May or June 2026. The ADN May 28 Fairbanks rate article does not mention U-25-028. No in-window published article naming U-25-028 was found. Gate 1 fails.
Alaska LNG Import Gas Supply Contract Jurisdiction Gap — FERC CP26-61-000 / AS 42.05.711(v)
regulatory · trigger: 2026-05-20		 diffuse_chokepoint and missing_primary_source_per_layer — Gate 5 fails: every candidate chokepoint resolves to a multi-member body (FERC multi-member federal commission, RCA five-commissioner panel, or Alaska Legislature). No single named officer holds an asymmetric binary over the mechanism's critical gate. Gate 3 partial failure: the Federal Register notice CP26-61-000 (L1 primary source) is CAPTCHA-blocked and its verbatim span could not be confirmed. Note: 15 U.S.C. § 717b(e)(1) was confirmed for FERC exclusive siting authority; SB 180 text and bill status on akleg.gov were confirmed for AS 42.05.711(v) and its legislative failure. The mechanism is structurally real but fails the asymmetric chokepoint gate.

Editor’s note

Run summary: All four scouts completed (no timeouts this cycle). The mapper ran successfully and applied the seven-point gate to all eight candidates. The 21-day broadening window was applied inline within the same mapper pass.

Closest candidates:

  • GCI AU-Aleutians Subsea Fiber (facilities, May 27 trigger) — Failed Gate 3: the FCC cable landing license settlement URL (L2) returned HTTP 503 on two attempts; the repair vessel dispatch layer (L3) had no contract or official document establishing the authority, only news articles.
  • Alaska LNG Import Gas Supply Jurisdiction Gap (regulatory, May 20 FERC docket) — Failed Gate 5: every candidate chokepoint resolves to a multi-member body (FERC, RCA five-commissioner panel, or Alaska Legislature). The mechanism is structurally real and consequential — AS 42.05.711(v) is an unrepealed clause left over from HB 50 (2024) that exempts FERC-jurisdictional LNG import facilities from RCA price oversight — but no single named officer holds the binary. Note for next cycle: if Governor Dunleavy adds SB 180 to a future special session scope (a single-person binary), that reframe may pass Gate 5.
  • Alaska Railbelt OATT — RCA Docket U-25-028 (regulatory) — Decision was due June 4, but no in-window published article named the docket. The RCA What’s New page carried no June 2026 U-25-028 entry. Watch for the actual RCA order, which may generate in-window coverage for the next cycle.

Strong future candidates (worth re-checking in coming cycles):

  • GCI-Quintillion FCC license transfer review — any FCC consent order or Team Telecom conditions expected Q3–Q4 2026 will generate fresh news-tie and may resolve the primary-source gaps that blocked both the cable break and BEAD novation mechanisms.
  • AS 42.05.711(v) / LNG jurisdiction gap — once the first Chugach Electric LNG supply contract is signed (post FERC authorization ~July 31, 2026), the RCA cost-recovery docket will open and provide an institutional primary-source chokepoint layer.
  • DAF EUL award announcement — evaluation of May 29 submissions is underway; any award announcement or source selection decision will provide a clean in-window news trigger.

No deviations to note beyond the no-target outcome itself. No scouts timed out. Mapper completed successfully. The LNG mechanism is the most promising target for the next run.
